book.readScope: Hair-loss narrative, finasteride, minoxidil and Latisse table entries read as extracted text and both full rendered pages. Adjacent eczema is not counted reviewed by this module.

readScope: All 11 final lessons, embedded checks, 11 visual definitions and renderer reviewed against the documented book and current sources. All original 112 questions read before replacement; all final 127 questions, choices, keys, rationales and anchors reread. Added reproductive/JAK counseling reconciled directly to current labels. Final integration checked regimen, population, thresholds, timing, off-label status and lesson/question/visual consistency.

findings.issue: No dedicated eyelash lesson in alopecia module; related glaucoma module has limited counseling.
findings.change: Added original eyelash lesson, embedded check, visual, primary label reference and eight assessment questions.

findings.issue: Book says no combined Latisse/glaucoma prostaglandin use.
findings.resolution: Current label requires consultation and IOP monitoring; formal contraindication is hypersensitivity. New lesson agrees with existing glaucoma module.

findings.issue: Minoxidil schedule/patient/product coverage is thin; blanket months-to-effect language can obscure OTC stop rules.
findings.status: Four labeled product regimens and nonresponse deadlines reconciled: men 5% solution 1 mL BID/4 months; women 5% foam half-cap QD/6 months; women 2% solution 1 mL BID/4 months; men 5% foam half-cap BID/4 months. Added exclusions and stop criteria. Book generic formulation summary expanded.

findings.issue: Severe alopecia areata JAK coverage lists drugs but omits selection-critical product-specific dosing, genotype and interaction details.
findings.status: Expanded baricitinib alopecia dosing, renal and OAT3 modifications; ritlecitinib dosing, missed-dose, platelet/ALC distinction, hepatic limits and interactions; existing deuruxolitinib additions retained.

findings.issue: Generic rotated assessment distractors may be unrelated true statements and rationales often do not address the tested dimension.
findings.status: All 112 original questions read and replaced with explicit original cases. Fifteen new cases added.

findings.issue: Finasteride assessment action overbroadly prohibited all handling in pregnancy; lesson omitted PSA interpretation and treated safety only as a list.
findings.change: Limited handling restriction to damaged tablets, explained intact coating and washing; expanded dose/time, PSA nadir, persistent sexual symptom reports, mood symptoms and context of higher-dose cancer studies. Do not infer lower sexual-event risk by comparing dissimilar 1 mg and 5 mg trials.

findings.issue: JAK expansion made one disease-recognition lesson carry too many separate prescribing decisions.
findings.change: Split exact JAK selection/monitoring into an eleventh lesson with its own original visual, embedded check and eight reassigned assessment anchors. Preserved alopecia-areata anchor for recognition/local treatment; added specialist alternatives and explicit off-label distinction for pediatric/AA minoxidil.

findings.issue: Minoxidil visual implied a fully established linear pathway to growth.
findings.change: Lesson and visual now distinguish experimental potassium-channel evidence from an incomplete clinical mechanism.

findings.issue: Book lists spironolactone as a medication-related alopecia contributor, while module lists it as off-label treatment without explaining the distinction.
findings.change: Verified alopecia reporting in current label; added association-versus-causation explanation plus pregnancy, contraindication, potassium and interaction safety.

findings.issue: Generic JAK monitoring and reproductive language obscured product-specific decisions.
findings.change: Added baricitinib AA CBC thresholds and twelve-week lipid assessment; deuruxolitinib renal/hepatic limits and inducer restrictions; exact post-dose breastfeeding intervals for all three agents, explicitly not contraception washouts; four original assessment cases. Source passages checked 2026-09-26.

findings.issue: Dutasteride named without developed evidence or safety teaching; SALT listed without interpretation.
findings.change: Added off-label US status, dual enzyme action, bounded 24-week randomized evidence, pregnancy handling, whole capsule administration, six-month blood-donation interval and selected monitoring/interactions. Clarified prostate-prevention trial doses to avoid implying dutasteride was studied above its usual 0.5 mg dose. Added SALT interpretation and three original assessment questions.

findings.issue: Book medication associations and endocrine/lupus/nutritional context incompletely named in lesson.
findings.change: Added label-supported clomiphene, hydroxychloroquine, peginterferon and contraceptive examples with causality limitations; added thyroid/menopause context and discoid-lupus scarring distinction; clarified deficiency-based supplementation and excess vitamin A/selenium harm.

findings.issue: Several assessment distractors were nonclinical or implausible; local steroid atrophy was tested without explicit lesson teaching.
findings.change: Revised seventeen choice sets while retaining IDs and correct keys; added local steroid adverse effects and fungal steroid-monotherapy caution to corresponding lessons. Full-bank reread completed; not a claim of pharmacist certification.

findings.issue: Eyelash lesson omitted pregnancy and lactation decision-making.
findings.change: Added original counseling based on Latisse sections 8.1 and 8.2: inadequate controlled pregnancy evidence, benefit-risk decision, unknown human milk exposure, and individualized maternal/infant considerations. No blanket contraindication or zero systemic exposure claim.

findings.issue: Generic JAK precautions did not teach several baricitinib-specific actions.
findings.change: Added viral-hepatitis screening, latent-TB treatment, shingles interruption, abdominal/perforation evaluation, thrombosis/hypersensitivity action, MI/stroke discontinuation, smoking risk and risk-based skin examination. Direct current label sections 5.1-5.10 reviewed.

findings.issue: Ritlecitinib counseling did not distinguish experimental loading arms from the approved regimen or cover common adverse reactions.
findings.change: Added no-loading-dose distinction, limited expectations at the trial endpoint, common adverse reactions and urgent allergy/thrombosis actions with skin-examination follow-up.

findings.issue: Deuruxolitinib teaching lacked several practical safety points and did not explicitly reject the experimental 12 mg dose.
findings.change: Added common adverse reactions, urgent abdominal/perforation evaluation, skin examination, thrombosis action and distinction between approved 8 mg twice daily and unapproved 12 mg trial arm.

sources.scope: Professional indication, full administration, contraindication, warnings, adverse reactions, special populations, mechanism, clinical tables and counseling through17 read. No efficacy percentages introduced. Patient insert/administration images remain to inspect if needed.
Women’s 5% foam Drug Facts: regimen, nonresponse deadline, exclusions and warnings read; enclosed booklet not yet reviewed.
Men’s 5% solution Drug Facts, updated March 4 2026: regimen, nonresponse, exclusions, warnings and trial limitations read.

Propecia sections 1-7 and pregnancy handling passages read; numerical trial tables not converted into comparative claims. Relevant teaching reconciled to label sections; full unrelated source coverage is not claimed. Current targeted closure: postmarketing psychiatric/sexual findings, damaged-tablet handling, trial withdrawal/response passages and patient counseling rechecked. Published trial percentages not adopted as patient guarantees.

June 2026 label, posted July 13 2026: highlights, boxed warning and full sections 1-5 read in earlier passes; follow-up closed sections 6-8, 10-14, 16 and 17, including adverse-event tables, interactions, reproductive/organ-function limits, pharmacogenomics and trial endpoints. No FDA-cleared/approved companion test currently described; CYP2C9 testing still required. 12 mg trial arm is unapproved. No cross-drug efficacy ranking, numerical adverse-event comparison, or universal response guarantee inferred. Figures and entire Medication Guide not claimed reviewed.

June 2026 label: highlights, boxed warning, sections 1-8, pharmacology including renal/hepatic and interaction tables, nonclinical sections 13.1-13.2, trial section 14, storage and professional counseling section 17 reviewed across documented passes. Follow-up read closed adverse-reaction table, trial and counseling gaps. Experimental loading arms distinguished from labeled 50 mg daily; SALT endpoint interpreted as residual scalp loss. Animal hearing findings not represented as an established human effect. Patient guide reviewed through allergy counseling, not claimed read in entirety.

June 2026 prescribing information: boxed warning, indications, dosage including AA-specific renal/CBC and OAT3 rules, full warnings 5.1-5.10, AA-specific adverse reactions and postmarketing section, interactions, targeted reproductive and organ-function passages, full AA trial section 14.3 and professional patient counseling reviewed. Follow-up closed the AA adverse-event and trial/counseling gaps. RA/COVID efficacy, complete nonclinical/pharmacokinetic sections and entire Medication Guide are not claimed reviewed; no claims drawn from those unreviewed sections. AA response at 36 weeks and down-titration follow-up do not imply universal response.

Diagnosis, observation, local corticosteroids, anthralin, off-label minoxidil, contact immunotherapy and systemic options through eyelash section reviewed. General AA minoxidil schedules are specialist-directed, not a replacement for OTC product labels.

Primary human follicle organ-culture, expression and immunohistology study abstract read. Supports channel involvement, not a complete proven clinical pathway. PMID2230218 search abstract supports sulfate activation but full page returned a challenge; do not claim full paper reviewed.
Diagnosis/biopsy, anti-inflammatory treatment, minoxidil adjunct, coexistence, hair-care and experimental-treatment distinction read. Added inflammatory-treatment goal to lesson.
CDC search-returned treatment guidance confirms systemic scalp treatment and warns steroids can worsen ringworm. No specific regimen introduced.
FDA assay-interference warning supports biotin laboratory reconciliation; no universal washout period or claim all assays are affected.

August 20 2026 label boxed warning and initial pharmacology read. Added oral exposure safety and distinguished labeled hypertension from off-label hair-loss use; no hypertension dose or mandatory adjunct extrapolated to alopecia.
Full Drug Facts and current carton text read for women 2% solution, including dose and four-month stop rule; no efficacy percentage adopted.
Full Drug Facts and carton text read for men 5% foam; half-cap twice daily and four-month stop rule.

March 2026 label indications, dosing context, contraindications, sections 5-8 including reported alopecia, interaction mechanisms and pregnancy/lactation read. No heart-failure dose extrapolated to hair loss.

Current posted Avodart label revised October 2023: indications/administration, pregnancy handling, PSA, prostate-cancer warning, semen/sexual adverse effects, CYP3A interactions, mechanism, persistence and counseling passages reviewed. No BPH efficacy claims or dosage extrapolation to other populations.
Entire primary trial abstract read, not full paper. Men 20-50, 917 randomized, 24-week endpoint; supports bounded hair-count/width claim, not long-term comparative safety.

Clinical overview read through prognosis: permanent follicular destruction, frontal/side band, brow and other body-hair loss; supports prompt recognition and treatment. No guarantee of regrowth or postmenopausal-only diagnosis introduced.
Full clinical narrative read: excessive tension, warning signs, permanent advanced loss, loosen/remove painful styling and dermatology review. Retained module teaching consistent.

Full clinical narrative read. Supports delayed stress/postpartum shedding, stopping contraceptive trigger and prescriber coordination. Do not adopt the patient page shorthand equating all nongrowing hair loss with anagen effluvium; module retains distinct mechanisms.
Clinical symptoms text read: frontal/temporal recession, eyebrow loss, itch/pain, scaly papules, facial and body-hair involvement. Supports retained recognition row; source photographs not reused.
Targeted relevant passages reviewed for AAD Hair-Loss Causes. Full label or whole source not claimed reviewed for unrelated treatment recommendations.

Targeted relevant passages reviewed for DailyMed Levonorgestrel/Ethinyl Estradiol Reports. Full label or whole source not claimed reviewed for unrelated treatment recommendations.
Professional adverse-reaction section read; does not list alopecia; lupus-like syndrome is explicitly described. Do not infer all lupus manifestations occur with drug-induced lupus.
Heparin adverse-reaction passages: delayed transient alopecia reported.
Warfarin section 6 read; alopecia listed under skin disorders. No causal incidence inferred.
Direct August 2024 label passages read: dermatologic adverse effects including atrophy and pigment changes, intralesional site/volume precautions. No procedure doses introduced.

Complete abstract delivered in search output after direct PubMed CAPTCHA. 90 randomized, 68 completed, oral 5 mg daily versus topical 5% twice daily for 24 weeks; no superiority for primary density endpoints, photographic vertex endpoint differed. Supports selected off-label use, not routine preference or long-term safety. No new dosing recommendation authored.

Diagnosis/early treatment read in prior pass; follow-up read minoxidil, devices, microneedling, procedures, prescription treatments, deficiency and expectations passages. Supports bounded retained procedure overview. Page updated December 2022: generic 6-12 month minoxidil expectation does not override current product-specific OTC nonresponse deadlines; broad spironolactone pregnancy wording does not override current label nuance. No quoted success rates adopted.

bookMedicationReconciliation.coveredExamples: Chemotherapy; anticoagulants; valproate/lithium; spironolactone; clomiphene; hydroxychloroquine; peginterferon alfa-2a; levonorgestrel-containing combined contraception; hormonal start/stop history. bookMedicationReconciliation.procainamide: RxPrep lists a hair-loss association. Directly reviewed current Pfizer adverse-reaction section does not list alopecia; focused primary-literature search did not identify a direct corroborating report. Resolution: retain the association in this discrepancy ledger as uncorroborated, do not teach it as established causation, and do not infer that label silence disproves a rare association. No treatment recommendation depends on that unconfirmed association.
